prompt: Which of the exported variables makes the AWS command line send its requests to moto instead of to Amazon?
hint: One of them names an address.

choices.text: `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`
choices.why: The region decides which regional address is used, and the address is still Amazon's.

choices.text: `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`
choices.why: Right. It replaces the address of every service with `http://localhost:4567`.

choices.text: `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, because moto only answers the key `test`
choices.why: The key signs the request; it does not say where the request goes. moto accepts any key, as the section on moto shows.

choices.text: `AWS_PAGER`
choices.why: That one only decides whether a long answer opens in `less`.

prompt: `aws sts get-caller-identity` answers with an account number that is not `123456789012`. What does that tell you?
hint: moto gives every account it imitates the same number.

choices.text: moto was restarted and generated a new account
choices.why: moto keeps the same example number across restarts; only its contents are forgotten.

choices.text: The region is not São Paulo
choices.why: An account number is the same in every region.

choices.text: The terminal holds real AWS credentials
choices.why: Right. Stop and find where the credentials came from before running anything else.

choices.text: The virtual environment is not active
choices.why: Without it `aws` still runs, since it lives in `~/.local/bin`; the account would still be moto's.

prompt: You stop moto with Ctrl+C at the end of a sitting and start it again the next day. What is in it?
hint: Where does moto keep what it is told?

choices.text: Nothing: it keeps everything in memory and starts empty
choices.why: Right. Each lesson rebuilds what it needs from its first command.

choices.text: Everything from the day before, which moto saved under `~/aws` when it stopped
choices.why: moto writes nothing to disk in this lab; stopping it forgets every bucket.

choices.text: The buckets, without their objects
choices.why: Buckets are forgotten with everything else.

prompt: A command answers `InvalidAccessKeyId: The AWS Access Key Id you provided does not exist in our records`. Which line of the setup is missing from that terminal?
hint: Who answered? moto accepts any key.

choices.text: The one that sets `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`
choices.why: Right. Without it the request went to the real AWS, which refused the key `test`.

choices.text: The one that sets the two keys to `test`
choices.why: With no keys at all the command line stops before sending anything, with `Unable to locate credentials`.

choices.text: The one that adds `~/.local/bin` to the path
choices.why: Without it, `aws` is not found and nothing is sent.

choices.text: The one that starts `moto_server` in the other terminal
choices.why: A stopped moto gives `Could not connect to the endpoint URL`, naming the local address.

prompt: Match each message to its cause.
hint: Read which program could have printed each one.

pairs.right: No key is set in this terminal

pairs.left: `Could not connect to the endpoint URL: "http://localhost:4567/"`

pairs.right: A moto is already listening on the port

prompt: In this lab, a listing signed with a key nobody issued succeeds. What does that show about moto by default?
hint: Compare it with the anonymous `curl`, which got 403.

choices.text: It checks that a request is signed, and not who signed it
choices.why: Right. And it evaluates no policy, so an action a policy should deny succeeds.

choices.text: It refuses every request that is not signed with the key `test`
choices.why: The listing was signed with another key and succeeded.

choices.text: It accepts any request, signed or not
choices.why: The unsigned `curl` was refused with 403.

choices.text: It forwards unknown keys to AWS to be checked
choices.why: moto never talks to AWS; the lab has no network in its captures at all.

prompt: An Athena query in moto comes back `SUCCEEDED` with 0 bytes scanned and no rows, against a table that does not exist. What is the right conclusion?
hint: What does moto do with SQL?

choices.text: The query is correct and the table is empty
choices.why: There is no table; Athena would have failed naming it.

choices.text: Athena creates a table the first time it is queried
choices.why: It does not; a query against a missing table is an error.

choices.text: Nothing about the SQL: moto records the request and runs no query
choices.why: Right. A success from moto means the request was well formed, and no more.

choices.text: The query was cached from an earlier run
choices.why: The answer says `ReusedPreviousResult: false`, and there was no earlier run.

prompt: Which of these does moto really do, rather than only record? Choose all that apply.
hint: The faithful services are the ones whose behaviour is a data structure.

choices.text: Keep the bytes of an S3 object and list keys by prefix
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Evaluate a DynamoDB conditional write
choices.why: Yes; the write is refused when the condition fails.

choices.text: Run the SQL of an Athena query
choices.why: It marks the query succeeded and runs nothing.

choices.text: Run the Spark code of a Glue job
choices.why: The job "succeeds" without a line being run.

choices.text: Send a bill for what was used
choices.why: moto has no prices; the price sheet does that part.

prompt: Where does every price this course quotes come from?
hint: moto reports none.

choices.text: From moto's billing interface
choices.why: moto has none.

choices.text: AWS's public price list, pinned per service
choices.why: Right. Pinned, so the sheet prints the same numbers next year.

choices.text: From the AWS Pricing API, which needs an account
choices.why: The price sheet reads public files and needs no account and no key.

choices.text: From the bill of the account the course was recorded on
choices.why: There is no account; the course was recorded against moto.

prompt: In the sheet, a GB-month of S3 Standard costs 0.04050 USD and one of Glacier Deep Archive costs 0.00320. How many times more is Standard? Round to the nearest whole number.
hint: Divide the two.

prompt: Why is a line of the price sheet not your bill?
hint: What else goes into an invoice?

choices.text: A bill is price × usage, plus tax, minus discounts
choices.why: Right. The sheet is the first factor of that product.

choices.text: The sheet is in USD and AWS bills Brazil in reais at a fixed rate
choices.why: The currency is a detail of payment; it does not turn a price into a bill.

choices.text: The sheet prints us-east-1 prices
choices.why: It reads sa-east-1, São Paulo.

prompt: `aws s3 ls s3://quitanda-raw-prod` shows `PRE raw/`, and `head-object` on the key `raw/orders/` answers 404. Why?
hint: What is a "folder" in a listing?

choices.text: The folder was deleted between the two commands
choices.why: Nothing was deleted; there was never an object with that key.

choices.text: No object has that key; `PRE` is a grouping
choices.why: Right. A folder is the answer to a question, not a thing that exists.

choices.text: Folders can only be read with `--recursive`
choices.why: `--recursive` lists the keys themselves; it does not make a folder an object.

choices.text: `head-object` refuses keys that end in a slash
choices.why: A key ending in a slash is legal, and the console's "Create folder" makes exactly one.

prompt: You append a line to a local file and upload it again to the same key. What happens to the object in an ordinary bucket, without versioning?
hint: S3 has no edit.

choices.text: S3 appends the new bytes to the end of the stored object
choices.why: There is no append; an object is written whole.

choices.text: The upload fails because the key already exists
choices.why: An overwrite is silent; nothing refuses it.

choices.text: A new object replaces it
choices.why: Right: a new ETag, and the old bytes are gone. Lesson 3 keeps them with versioning.

choices.text: S3 keeps both under the same key and returns the newest
choices.why: That is what versioning does, and it is off unless turned on.

prompt: For an object uploaded in a single request, the ETag S3 returns is the ___ of its bytes.
hint: `md5sum` printed the same 32 characters.

prompt: Which of these would AWS refuse as the name of a general-purpose bucket? Choose all that apply.
hint: Lowercase, digits, hyphens and dots; 3 to 63; not an address.

choices.text: `Quitanda_Raw`
choices.why: A capital letter and an underscore, both refused.
A name shaped like an IP address is refused.

choices.text: `qr`
choices.why: Two characters; the minimum is three.

choices.text: `quitanda-raw-prod`
choices.why: Valid, if nobody has it yet.

choices.text: `quitanda-logs-dev`
choices.why: Valid too.

prompt: `quitanda.raw.prod` is a legal bucket name. Why does this course avoid dots anyway?
hint: Think of the address `bucket.s3.sa-east-1.amazonaws.com` and its certificate.

choices.text: HTTPS to the usual address fails its certificate check
choices.why: Right. The wildcard certificate covers one label, and the dots make three.

choices.text: Dots make the name longer than the 63 characters a bucket name is allowed
choices.why: A dot is one character like a hyphen.

choices.text: S3 reads each dot in a bucket's name as one more level of folder
choices.why: Folders come from slashes in keys, not from a bucket's name.

choices.text: moto refuses dotted names
choices.why: It accepted `quitanda.raw.prod` in the capture.

prompt: Why does the key layout write `dt=2026-10-01` rather than `dt=01-10-2026`?
hint: In what order does S3 return keys?

choices.text: S3 refuses dates with the day first
choices.why: A key may hold almost anything; nothing refuses it.

choices.text: Byte order then equals time order
choices.why: Right. S3 lists keys in byte order, and day first would list every first of the month together.

choices.text: Athena only reads partitions written year first
choices.why: Athena reads a partition value as a string, whatever its shape; the order is a matter of listing.

prompt: Which of these belongs in a bucket name, by the scheme of this lesson?
hint: Company, layer, environment.

choices.text: The name of the engineer who created it
choices.why: People move and the bucket stays.

choices.text: The environment it serves, such as `prod` or `dev`
choices.why: Right. It keeps test data out of production buckets.

choices.text: The name of the customer whose data it holds
choices.why: A bucket name travels in DNS and in error messages; nothing personal goes in it.

choices.text: The date the bucket was created
choices.why: The date is a property of the data, and it goes in the keys.

prompt: Put the steps of a sitting of this course in order.
hint: The server comes first, in its own terminal.
items: Start `moto_server -p 4567` in a terminal of its own
Open a second terminal and run the four lines of "Every time you open a terminal"
Check with `aws sts get-caller-identity` that the account is `123456789012`
Run the lesson's commands, which rebuild what it needs

prompt: Quitanda wants to "rename" the prefix `raw/orders/` to `raw/sales/` across 40,000 objects. What does that take in S3?
hint: There is no rename and no directory.

choices.text: One request that renames the folder
choices.why: There is no folder to rename.

choices.text: A copy and a delete for each object: 80,000 requests
choices.why: Right, and every reader of the old keys breaks. Which is why keys are written as if they could never be renamed.

choices.text: Changing the bucket's prefix setting
choices.why: A bucket has no such setting.

choices.text: A copy of each object, after which S3 deletes the originals
choices.why: S3 deletes nothing on its own; the deletes are 40,000 more requests.
